name: Mental Maths Foundations
description: A high-utility mental-maths deck covering number bonds, complements, bridging through 10 and 100, left-to-right addition, compensation, counting up, doubles, near-doubles, double-and-half, and method-selection practice. It teaches when a method is appropriate, not just the final shortcut.
estimatedTime: 150–210 minutes for a first focused pass; then short daily review sessions

cards.term: What are number bonds, and why do they matter in mental maths?
cards.definition:
Number bonds are pairs of numbers that make a useful target such as 10, 20, 50, 100, or 1000.

Examples:
6 + 4 = 10
37 + 63 = 100
248 + 752 = 1000

They let you regroup numbers quickly instead of calculating digit by digit.

cards.term: How do you subtract a number from 9, 99, or 999 quickly?
cards.definition:

cards.term: How do you choose a mental-maths method?
cards.definition:
Ask one question first:
What friendly number, bond, double, or place-value split is hiding here?

Examples:
84 − 29 → compensate with 30
48 + 37 → compensate with 50
503 − 487 → count upward
247 + 132 → split 132 by place value
24 × 125 → double-and-half

cards.term: Choose the best primary method for: 48 + 37
cards.definition:
Best method: Addition compensation

Why:
Round 48 to 50, then subtract 2.

Other methods may work, but this one usually has the lowest cognitive load.

cards.term: Choose the best primary method for: 84 − 29
cards.definition:
Best method: Subtraction compensation

Why:
Subtract 30, then add 1 back.

Other methods may work, but this one usually has the lowest cognitive load.

cards.term: Choose the best primary method for: 503 − 487
cards.definition:
Best method: Counting up

Why:
The gap is small and 500 is a convenient bridge.

Other methods may work, but this one usually has the lowest cognitive load.

cards.term: Choose the best primary method for: 347 + 286
cards.definition:
Best method: Left-to-right addition

Why:
Split 286 into 200 + 80 + 6.

Other methods may work, but this one usually has the lowest cognitive load.

cards.term: Choose the best primary method for: 24 × 125
cards.definition:
Best method: Double-and-half

Why:
Halve 24 and double 125 until 1000 appears.

Other methods may work, but this one usually has the lowest cognitive load.

cards.term: Choose the best primary method for: 97 + 68
cards.definition:

Other methods may work, but this one usually has the lowest cognitive load.

cards.term: Choose the best primary method for: 1000 − 248
cards.definition:

Why:

Other methods may work, but this one usually has the lowest cognitive load.
